title: Teaching & Mentoring
text:
I see teaching and mentoring as a shared construction of knowledge rather than a one-way transfer. Students bring their own experiences, questions and realities to the classroom, and learning works best when it starts from them and leads to critical, independent thinking.
In my group I favor teamwork over individual competition: students help each other and draw on each person’s different abilities. We meet weekly or biweekly to discuss progress, calibrate ideas and solve problems together, and I give the most support to those who need it most. Mentoring is, for me, the best way to build critical reasoning, organization and collaboration skills — and to explore new ideas.
A core principle of my mentoring is that theses and dissertations should become peer-reviewed papers. Around 90% of my mentees have published their thesis work, which strengthens their careers, benefits their graduate programs, and returns the results of publicly funded research to society.
I have taught and mentored in more than six graduate and undergraduate programs, across very different social and educational contexts in Argentina, Brazil, and beyond.

title: Research
text: My research asks where species live, how that will change, and how we can use that knowledge to conserve them. I combine field-based knowledge of Neotropical vegetation with spatial modelling, data science, and software development.

title: Research
text:
Research lines


Species distribution models: methods & best practices
How far can a model be extrapolated? How do we deal with overprediction, temporal mismatches or abundance data? I develop and test methods that make species distribution models more reliable (e.g., the Shape extrapolation metric, overprediction corrections, abundance-based models).
Velazco et al. 2023 Ecography · Velazco et al. 2020 Biol. Conserv.


Conservation biogeography & protected areas
I evaluate how well protected areas and other area-based measures safeguard species, phylogenetic diversity, and the uses people make of biodiversity, and I identify priority areas — including across national borders.
Velazco et al. 2023 Biol. Conserv. · Velazco et al. 2022 Biol. Conserv.


Global change: climate, land use & fire
I forecast how climate change, land-use change, and shifting fire regimes affect plants and animals — from the Cerrado flora and Neotropical palms to plants in the California Floristic Province.
Velazco et al. 2019 Divers. Distrib. · Syphard et al. 2024 PNAS


Biodiversity models for policy
Through iDiv’s sModelProBio and the EcoCode working group, I help coordinate model intercomparisons that inform the Global Biodiversity Framework.
Zurell et al. 2025 PNAS · Urban et al. 2026 Nat. Ecol. Evol.


Open-source tools for biodiversity science
I write R (and soon Python) packages so that cleaning biodiversity data and building species distribution models is transparent, reproducible and accessible.
See my software →


Neotropical forests & flora
My roots are in forest engineering: floristics, structure, and dynamics of the Atlantic Forest, Araucaria forest, and savannas of Misiones and southern Brazil.
Velazco et al. 2018 Rodriguésia

title: Santiago José Elías Velazco
text:
Hi! I am a Research Scientist at the Center for Open Geographical Science (COGS), San Diego State University (USA), and an Assistant Researcher at the Subtropical Biology Institute (IBS, CONICET–UNaM), Argentina.
My work sits at the intersection of conservation ecology, biogeography, and spatial modelling. I develop and apply species distribution models to understand how climate change, land use and fire shape biodiversity, and to help decide where and how to protect it. I also build open-source tools —such as flexsdm, adm and bdc— so that robust biodiversity modelling is accessible to everyone.
I have taught and mentored students in graduate programs across Argentina, Brazil, and beyond, and I co-lead the EcoCode working group on biodiversity modelling.

title: Bio
text:
I am an Argentinean ecologist working on conservation ecology, conservation biogeography, and spatial models.
I graduated in Forest Engineering from the National University of Misiones, Argentina (2010), where I was distinguished as an Outstanding Graduate of the Faculty of Forestry Sciences. I then earned a Master’s (2014) and a Ph.D. (2018) in Forest Engineering, in the nature conservation research line, at the Federal University of Paraná, Brazil.
I was a postdoctoral researcher at the Subtropical Biology Institute (UNaM–CONICET, Argentina; 2018–2021) and at the University of California, Riverside (USA; 2021–2022), supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation. Today I work as a Researcher at the Subtropical Biology Institute (CONICET–UNaM, Argentina) and as a Research Scientist at the Center for Open Geographical Science, San Diego State University (USA).
I have supervised students and taught courses in graduate programs in Argentina and Brazil, and I co-lead the EcoCode working group on biodiversity modelling.
